correctness.rationale: For every subgroup generated by a tetrahedral permutation, fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on primitive Hasse-edge orbits; the canonical orbit-complex geometric realization is therefore PL-homeomorphic to the actual geometric fixed locus. Exhaustive enumeration over at most ten admissible orbits yields the four exact face vectors. A standalone checker compares reversed-Hasse topological sort with fixed-dimensional closed-gradient-path acyclicity on every tested subset, checks 60 actual free-face collapses to the exact six-vertex octahedral boundary, checks two four-cycles in the double-transposition case, the filled triangle for the three-cycle and no admissible vertex for the four-cycle, and checks all 24 tetrahedral permutations. The 28 original Hasse relations match the source and the fixed-simplex counts agree with published independent character enumeration. The theorem relies on finite exhaustive proof, not numerical inference.

value.rationale: This classifies four canonical geometric symmetry-fixed subspaces of a newly studied nontrivial 99-sphere-wedge Morse complex. It identifies an actual two-sphere, a disconnected pair of circles, a contractible fixed set and an empty fixed set, while the existing rational character gives only their Euler numbers. In particular, disconnected double-transposition fixed points and the 60-step collapse to an octahedron are structural topological data relevant to the equivariant Morse-complex space of gradient choices. The four conjugacy types exhaust all nonidentity tetrahedral symmetries; this is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary subcase.
